newsitem.title: CUBA: Havana hotels hit by corruption, theft.
newsitem.headline: Havana hotels hit by corruption, theft.

text.p: Corruption and theft, sometimes implicating members of the ruling Communist Party, have been uncovered at several leading Havana hotels, Cuban officials said on Tuesday.

A report in the Communist Party newspaper Granma on a meeting this week of the party branch in the central Havana district of Plaza de la Revolucion said the director of one hotel, the Vedado, had been dismissed.

In addition, three party members had been expelled and 11 had been disciplined by temporary expulsion because of problems at the hotel. The paper did not say what these problems had been, other than that it had been a serious case that should serve as example.

But it added that party officials working at the Hotel Nacional, the Hotel Cohiba and the Hotel Libre-Tryp had told the meeting of the "complex battle that party militants have to wage in these places, where there have been regrettable incidents of corruption, theft and other negative behaviour, in which party members have been implicated."
The hotels are the top three in Havana.

The newspaper did not give details of these incidents or say when they had taken place but representatives of foreign companies in the tourism sector have said that robbery, not of guests but of hotel property, is a possible problem in hotels.

Hotel workers are generally far better off than other Cubans because they have access to tips in hard currency. But there is still a temptation to steal because workers are in contact with goods such as food not readily available.
The Havana meeting also discussed delays in work renovating the Havana Libre-Tryp, a state-owned hotel that Spanish hotel chain Tryp has recently begun managing.
